exec_summary: Site traffic (GA4, 2026-04-04 to 2026-04-10): growthbook.io had 9,913 sessions and 6,412 users (-16.8% week over week).

GrowthBook clicks dropped 29% week over week, from 4,777 to 3,377. Critically, the homepage alone accounts for 1,039 of the 1,400 lost clicks -- this is branded search fluctuation on the root domain, not a content or ranking collapse across the site. Pricing also slipped 25 clicks and the experiments product page dropped 10, which are worth watching but are not alarming on their own. Comparison page data is unavailable this week, so we cannot draw conclusions there.

The single most important strategic finding this week is Harness publishing content on warehouse-native experimentation reaching general availability. Warehouse-native experimentation is a capability buyers are actively evaluating, and Harness staking a GA claim gives them a concrete, search-ready differentiator. GrowthBook has no visible content answering 'warehouse-native experimentation' queries, which means we are invisible at a moment when this category is being defined.

On the competitor front, Optimizely published on experimentation messaging and roadmap -- a tier-1 threat targeting buyers mid-funnel who are comparing platforms. Amplitude Experiment dropped a customer case study showing a 4x increase in experimentation volume at Defacto, a format that ranks well and builds bottom-funnel trust. Unleash published on how AI changes feature experimentation for product teams, going after the agentic/AI angle that is gaining search momentum. PostHog pushed new React Router SDK docs for both experiments and feature flags, reinforcing their developer-first positioning in a high-KD (55) keyword cluster.
content_recommendations: 1. Write a dedicated page on 'warehouse-native experimentation' because Harness just announced GA on this topic and GrowthBook has zero visible content targeting those queries -- this is a category-defining moment and we are absent.

2. Write a customer case study modeled on the Defacto/Amplitude format showing a GrowthBook customer scaling experimentation volume, because Amplitude Experiment is building bottom-funnel trust with this format (rank 4 opportunity, scored 70) and GrowthBook has no comparable asset.

3. Expand GrowthBook's content on 'bayesian statistics in experimentation' because this is ranked as the #2 opportunity this week (score 75) and Amplitude Experiment already owns this topic -- GrowthBook's stats engine is a core differentiator and we should be winning these queries.

4. Refresh or create content targeting 'feature flag testing' because Flagsmith is capturing this query (rank 5, score 70) and it is a direct Content Gap for GrowthBook -- this is a high-intent term for developers evaluating feature flag platforms.

5. Optimize GrowthBook's React Router SDK docs or write a focused integration guide, because PostHog published four separate React Router installation pages this week across experiments, feature flags, session replay, and web analytics -- all targeting KD 55 keywords where developer-focused install guides tend to rank quickly.
